text:
ajohnson: Quick question — I'm prototyping a small 'rollback-gateway' shim to handle tenant-level fallthrough during canary / A-B rollouts. Want design feedback.

maria-chen: Nice. What's the failure model we need to cover? full outage, high-error-rate, or tail-latency degradation?

ajohnson: All of the above ideally. Primary goal: automatic, transparent switchback to baseline variant per-tenant with minimal client changes. Also want clear audit telemetry.

ryan: +1. Implementation idea: a gateway service that evaluates per-request policies (tenant config, latency SLO, error rate) and makes routing decision. If it falls back, attach X-Redwood-Fallback: <reason>.

sasha: How do we prevent cascading fallback storms? If many tenants flip at once, baseline could get overloaded. Need token-bucket or circuit per-tenant + global backpressure.

maria-chen: Agree. Also we should provide a soft-lease: fallback windows that auto-expire unless operator confirms. That helps avoid permanent silent routing changes.

ajohnson: Sketch of decision surface:
```
decision = {
  tenant_policy: enum(allow, opt-out, force-baseline),
  latency_budget_ms: 200,
  error_rate_pct: 2.0,
  sliding_window_secs: 60
}
```
Gateway polls health probes + downstream metrics and evaluates every 10s.

ryan: For metrics ingestion, push per-tenant aggregates (qps, p95, error-rate) into rollout-signal table. Keep evaluation deterministic and idempotent.

sam-lee: Question: where does rollout ownership live? Should rollout controller write desired state to tenant metadata and gateway just reads it, or should gateway own transient state (leases)?

ajohnson: My thinking: rollout controller writes desired policy and probes. Gateway keeps ephemeral lease records for active fallback decisions (so it can timebox and avoid thrashing). Leasing table with TTLs.

sasha: Can we reuse the existing circuit-service? It already has per-tenant circuits and cooldown timers. If gateway uses that and only holds a short lease, we avoid duplicating logic.

maria-chen: Telemetry requirements: emit event on every decision with fields {tenant, route_taken, reason, prev_variant, new_variant, trigger_metrics}. These feed the rollout dashboard + alerts.

ryan: Also add an API for manual override: POST /tenants/:id/rollback with body {duration, reason}. That should create an auditable entry.

ajohnson: Nice. One tricky edge: state drift when gateway restarts. Lease TTLs + idempotent reconciliation should cover it. Also fallback decisions must be conservative on startup (start in baseline until warmed).

devops-bot: deploy rollback-gateway v0.3 -> success :white_check_mark: (canary -> 10% traffic)

sam-lee: Ops note — when enabling, recommend reserve headroom on baseline cluster (20%) and add alert if baseline CPU > 70% after fallback.

ajohnson: Thanks all. Next steps: I'll draft a short RFC with interfaces (tenant-policy schema, lease table schema, event format) and a minimal reference implementation that delegates circuits to circuit-service. Posting draft in #eng-platform tomorrow.

maria-chen: Thanks! Also add a test plan: chaos test that kills variant nodes and ensures fallback remains bounded and observable.

sasha: +1 to chaos tests. Also include a load test that simulates 100 tenants flipping simultaneously.

ryan: I'll add the dashboard panels and alerting playbook after the RFC.

ajohnson: Sweet — will ping when RFC is up. :rocket:
